title: Fresh Herb Gravy
summary: A shallot roux simmered with beef stock and woody herbs, strained smooth and brightened with fresh herbs.

ingredients.note: low-salt; contains celery in most brands

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the shallots
steps.text: Melt the butter over medium heat and cook the shallots for about 4 min until soft.

steps.title: Make the roux
steps.text: Add the flour and stir for 4-5 min until light brown.

steps.title: Infuse the herbs
steps.text: Whisk in the hot stock, drop in the thyme sprigs, rosemary and bay leaf, and simmer for 10 min until the gravy coats a spoon.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through the sieve into a clean pan or jug, pressing the shallots to extract their flavour. Discard the stalks and leaves.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the chopped parsley and thyme leaves, season with salt and pepper and serve hot with sliced roast chicken.

tips: Bruise the herb sprigs lightly before adding to release their oils.
Add sage leaves with the thyme for a stuffing-like flavour.
Keep the gravy warm over low heat but add the fresh herbs at the last minute.
Use a little roast chicken resting juice for extra flavour.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat until piping hot and add fresh herbs again if you like. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
